title: Realization of decoherence-induced averaged symmetry-protected topological phases on quantum processors
authors: Ruizhe Shen, Xue-Jia Yu, Ching Hua Lee
abstract: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases are conventionally formulated for pure states protected by exact symmetries. In open quantum systems, however, decoherence generates mixed-state ensembles in which average symmetry can instead emerge only after averaging over microscopic trajectories. In this work, we realize decoherence-induced averaged SPT (ASPT) order on programmable quantum processors. Starting from a one-dimensional cluster SPT, we engineer sublattice-selective Pauli-$Z$ dephasing through ancilla-assisted quantum circuits. We observe the resulting symmetry conversion through the decay of the symmetry charge. Moreover, a two-replica Renyi-2 string correlator measured through destructive SWAP readout remains nontrivial, revealing the ASPT structure encoded at the density-matrix level. We further show that the engineered dephasing redistributes spectral weight among reduced-stabilizer sectors while preserving the characteristic twofold pairing of the half-chain entanglement spectrum. These results establish a gate-based route to engineering and probing ASPT order and demonstrate structured decoherence as a programmable resource for realizing mixed-state topological quantum matter.
summary: This paper demonstrates how to engineer and measure decoherence-induced averaged symmetry-protected topological (ASPT) phases on quantum processors. By applying controlled dephasing, the authors convert a pure-state topological order into a mixed-state order, proving that structured decoherence itself can be a resource for realizing complex quantum matter states.
main_problem: The primary goal is to realize and characterize decoherence-induced averaged symmetry-protected topological (ASPT) phases, moving beyond traditional pure-state SPT formulations.
main_result: The authors establish a gate-based route to engineer and probe ASPT order, demonstrating that structured decoherence can act as a programmable resource for realizing mixed-state topological quantum matter.
method: The study uses engineered local Pauli-Z dephasing on a 1D cluster SPT state, diagnosing the resulting mixed state using two-replica Renyi-2 string correlators and analyzing the reduced-density-matrix entanglement spectrum.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional cluster SPT state implemented on programmable quantum processors. The physics involves transitioning from pure-state SPT order to mixed-state ASPT order via controlled decoherence.
key_observables: Symmetry charge decay ($Q_{	ext{even}}$), two-replica Renyi-2 string correlator ($C^{(2)}_{i,k}$), and the half-chain reduced-density-matrix spectrum.
important_parameters: Dephasing probability ($p$), system length ($L$), and the structure of the engineered dephasing channel (sublattice-selective Pauli-Z dephasing).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ability to implement controlled, local dephasing channels and the use of advanced diagnostics like the two-replica correlator to confirm order at the density-matrix level.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the process from pure SPT to mixed ASPT via dephasing, and show hardware measurements of the symmetry charge decay and single-copy string order suppression.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the concept of ASPT phases, then details the experimental realization using engineered dephasing on a cluster state, followed by rigorous diagnostics using two-replica correlators and entanglement spectrum analysis, contrasting this with measurement-and-feedback protocols.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the challenge of characterizing topological order in realistic, noisy quantum hardware, which is a major frontier in condensed matter theory and quantum computation.
